headline: You got a triamcinolone injection in your right knee, and Dr. Okafor plans to check how long it helped around February 2026.

followUps.title: Book your knee follow-up
followUps.detail: See Dr. Okafor around February 2026 to review how long the injection helped.

instructions.text: Take it easy for the first 48 hours after the injection. Skip long walks. If your knee is sore, use ice for 15 minutes a few times a day. Go back to your home exercises after the 48 hours.
Over the next few days, call Dr. Okafor’s office right away if your knee gets hot, red, or very swollen, or if you get a fever.
Keep moving. Dr. Okafor said a short walk every day is good for your knee.
You can get another knee injection, but not more often than every 3 months.

unchanged.text: Keep taking your blood pressure medicine as usual.
Keep using acetaminophen as before if you need it: up to 2 tablets three times a day. Do not take more than 6 tablets (3,000 mg) in a day.
Your home exercises are still the most important part of treatment, even if the injection makes your knee feel much better.

openQuestions.text: How long will the injection ease your knee pain?
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: Dr. Okafor will review this at your follow-up around February 2026.
